# 2025_Q53

## Question

The marked structure in the laryngoscopic image is:

## Options

- A) Thyroid cartilage
- B) Pyriform sinus ✅
- C) Epiglottis
- D) Vallecula

## Your Answer

C) Epiglottis

## Correct Answer

B) Pyriform sinus

## Key Fact (generated by LLM)

The marked structure in the laryngoscopic image is the pyriform sinus, which is a small recess on either side of the laryngeal entrance, formed by the aryepiglottic fold. The pyriform sinus is an important landmark in laryngoscopy, as it helps to identify the vocal cords and the entrance to the trachea. The epiglottis, on the other hand, is a flap-like structure that separates the trachea from the esophagus and is located above the vocal cords.

## Why You Got It Wrong (generated by LLM)

The student incorrectly identified the epiglottis as the marked structure, likely due to its prominent appearance in laryngoscopic images. This mistake suggests a lack of understanding of the anatomy of the larynx.
